section_summary: This section moves from a June 1945 intelligence memorandum on wartime shortages and civilian conditions in Japan to reports on the emperor, Japanese Communism, Soviet views of Japan’s ruling classes, and the Japanese Liberation League. The post-surrender material concentrates on political prisoners, occupation-era governmental reform, requests for biographical intelligence, and the emergence of Liberal, Socialist, and Communist parties. It concludes with two filed copies of a detailed report on Japanese political parties and a later declassification form.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Conditions in Wartime Japan Reported by a Returned Chinese Student
subfiles.from: B. E. R., Second Secretary on detail at Xi'an, Shaanxi
subfiles.about: Reports a Chinese student's observations of economic, social, military, educational, and transportation conditions in wartime Japan.
subfiles.summary: Returned Chinese student describes severe rationing, nutritional disease, shortages, taxes, bond purchases, air-raid fear, POW labor, closed colleges, and his journey through Korea and Manchuria.

subfiles.title: Political Association to Hear Report on Emperor's Health and on Foreign Affairs
subfiles.from: H. Kullgren, Department of State
subfiles.about: Analyzes a Tokyo broadcast announcing speeches on the emperor's health and Japanese foreign policy.
subfiles.summary: Great Japan Political Association to hear Shimomura on the emperor's health and Togo on foreign affairs; the meeting might boost morale at Potsdam or prepare a justification for surrender.

subfiles.title: Navy Memorandum Forwarding Information on Akamatsu, Matsumoto, Yuasa, Inouye, Ishigaki, Matsui, Fujii, and Hasegawa
subfiles.from: Wallace S. Wharton, Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon, attention John K. Emmerson
subfiles.about: Forwards eight naval intelligence biographical summaries requested by the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Navy memorandum answers a July 23, 1945 request: seven summaries on named individuals and no record for Taiji Hasegawa.

subfiles.title: Summary of Information on Saburō Akamatsu
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon and John K. Emmerson
subfiles.about: Provides intelligence on Saburō Akamatsu's education, residence, religious work, and organizational connections.
subfiles.summary: Badly degraded summary on Saburo Akamatsu: education in Japan and America, career as a pastor, and residence information.

subfiles.title: Summary of Information on Tōru Matsumoto
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon and John K. Emmerson
subfiles.about: Summarizes Tōru Matsumoto's family, ordination, education, marriage, and residence.
subfiles.summary: Heavily damaged summary identifies Toru Matsumoto as an ordained religious figure with New York ties.

subfiles.title: Summary of Information on Hachirō Yuasa
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon and John K. Emmerson
subfiles.about: Reviews Hachirō Yuasa's scientific education, employment, and activities in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Summary on Hachiro Yuasa: entomology study, newspaper work, arrival in the US and contacts on Japanese relocation.

subfiles.title: Summary of Information on Kakutarō Inouye
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon and John K. Emmerson
subfiles.about: Provides biographical and immigration information on Kakutarō Inouye.
subfiles.summary: Damaged summary on Kakutaro Inouye: Hokkaido, Yale, Heidelberg, study periods, US entry and associations.

subfiles.title: Summary of Information on Eitarō Ishigaki
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon and John K. Emmerson
subfiles.about: Summarizes Eitarō Ishigaki's work, immigration status, and alleged political associations.
subfiles.summary: Fragments on Eitaro Ishigaki: alien registration, possible departure from the US, and alleged Communist associations.

subfiles.title: Summary of Information on Ayako Ishigaki, Also Known as Haru Matsui
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon and John K. Emmerson
subfiles.about: Profiles writer and lecturer Ayako Ishigaki and evaluates her political associations.
subfiles.summary: Summary on Ayako Ishigaki (Haru Matsui): born Tokyo 1903, entered the US in 1926, writer, married Eitaro Ishigaki, opposed Japan's military regime; alleged Communist-affiliated contacts.

subfiles.title: Summary of Information on Ryōichi Fujii
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon and John K. Emmerson
subfiles.about: Records Ryōichi Fujii's birth, schooling, university education, languages, and U.S. residence.
subfiles.summary: Summary on Ryoichi Fujii: born in Kyoto, educated there and at Oberlin, degrees in philosophy and religion, speaks Japanese, English and German.

subfiles.title: Summary of Information on Taiji Hasegawa
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon and John K. Emmerson
subfiles.about: States that naval intelligence had no record for Taiji Hasegawa.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure contains only Hasegawa's name and the statement “No record.” No biographical information is supplied.

subfiles.title: Request for Translation of Sokolov's “Ruling Classes of Japan”
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests an airmail translation of Sokolov's article in Red Fleet.
subfiles.summary: Department asks for the full translated text of Sokolov's 'Ruling Classes of Japan' (Moscow telegram 3127).

subfiles.title: Rome Airgram A-666 on the Japanese Communist Party
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy, Rome
subfiles.about: Summarizes an L'Unità article on Susumu Okano and the wartime activities and program of the Japanese Communist Party.
subfiles.summary: The article claims the party survived severe repression, organized underground resistance, and cooperated with other democratic and anti-militarist groups. Okano is quoted as favoring a referendum on the imperial institution if the Japanese public wished to retain it, while predicting a central Communist role in postwar democracy.

subfiles.title: Moscow Telegram 3127 on Sokolov's “Ruling Classes of Japan”
subfiles.from: W. Averell Harriman, U.S. Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Soviet critique of Japan's constitutional and ruling-class structure.
subfiles.summary: Sokolov depicts the constitution, parliament, Privy Council, and political parties as instruments of landlords, capitalists, former feudal lords, and militarists. The embassy regards the article as a useful outline of Soviet political objections likely to shape Moscow's reaction to Japan's occupation government.

subfiles.title: Moscow Telegram 3142 on Owen Lattimore's Warning About Japanese Political Maneuvers
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.about: Reports Pravda's summary of Owen Lattimore's claims that Japan sought to divide the Allies.
subfiles.summary: Lattimore argues that Japan hoped to exploit the emperor, Chinese right-wing elements, and divisions among China, the Soviet Union, the United States, and Britain. He warns that inconsistent Allied policy would allow Japan to retain political initiative and obstruct improved Soviet-Chinese relations.

subfiles.title: Moscow Airgram A-245 on Okano and the Emperor Question
subfiles.from: George F. Kennan, U.S. Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.about: Assesses the conflict between Japanese Communist tactics and Soviet hostility toward retaining the emperor.
subfiles.summary: Kennan notes Okano long accepted temporary retention of the emperor; the Japanese party faces a dilemma as Soviet press criticized the American decision.

subfiles.title: Moscow Airgram A-247 on the Japanese Countryside
subfiles.from: George F. Kennan, U.S. Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Red Star article attributing Japanese rural poverty to landlordism rather than natural land scarcity.
subfiles.summary: The article argues that concentrated ownership, high rents, and backward agrarian relations impoverished peasants and supplied cheap labor and soldiers for imperial expansion. It calls for serious land reform as essential to agricultural recovery, demilitarization, and genuine democratization.

subfiles.title: Navy Memorandum Forwarding Material on the Japanese Liberation League
subfiles.from: Wallace S. Wharton
subfiles.about: Forwards a Fourteenth Naval District intelligence memorandum on the Japanese Liberation League.
subfiles.summary: Wharton sends the September 11 Navy memorandum on the Japanese Liberation League for State's retention; the FBI knew of it.

subfiles.title: Fourteenth Naval District Memorandum on the Japanese Liberation League
subfiles.from: H. S. Burr, District Intelligence Officer, Fourteenth Naval District
subfiles.about: Forwards the League's draft principles and bylaws because of their intelligence interest.
subfiles.summary: Fourteenth Naval District memo: Japanese Liberation League headquartered at Yan'an, Communist-based, led by Susumu Okano.

subfiles.title: Draft Outlines Covering General Principles of the Japanese Liberation League
subfiles.from: Japanese Liberation League
subfiles.about: Sets out the League's program for ending the war and constructing a democratic, demilitarized, and socially reformed Japan.
subfiles.summary: The program demands immediate peace, withdrawal from occupied territories, punishment of war leaders, abolition of conscription and military privilege, economic reconstruction, land reform, civil liberties, universal adult suffrage, and improved labor and military-service conditions. It concludes by advocating the overthrow of the wartime government and formation of a broad people's government representing progressive parties and organizations.

subfiles.title: Draft By-Laws of the Japanese Liberation League and Its North China Regional Council
subfiles.from: Japanese Liberation League
subfiles.about: Defines the League's membership, governing bodies, regional hierarchy, finances, discipline, and North China organization.
subfiles.summary: The bylaws establish a representatives' general meeting, Central Committee, regional and district councils, branches, cells, and affiliated organizations, with provisions for legal and clandestine activity. The North China council is headquartered in Yan'an and operates through annual conferences and committees, while an appendix maps the hierarchy and temporarily assigns central authority to a preparatory committee.

subfiles.title: Paris Telegram 5760 on Imprisoned Japanese Communists
subfiles.from: Jefferson Caffery, U.S. Embassy, Paris
subfiles.about: Reports French Communist-influenced press claims that ten thousand Communists remained imprisoned in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Paris telegram: Libres names jailed Japanese Communist leaders; L'Humanité links the party's silence to Soviet demands for a common Allied line and criticizes American practices.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Report on Release of Japanese Political Prisoners
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.to: George Atcheson, Political Adviser to SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests information on occupation action to release Japanese political prisoners.
subfiles.summary: Department says many Japanese political prisoners were reportedly not freed and asks the political adviser what measures were taken.

subfiles.title: Airgram Forwarding Biographical Information on Japanese Personalities
subfiles.from: James F. Byrnes, Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Political Adviser to the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Transmits biographical information on a list of Japanese military, diplomatic, and political figures.
subfiles.summary: Airgram answering Tokyo telegram 19 sends biographical intelligence on Japanese personalities, including Hashimoto, Kimura, Kurusu and Nomura.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram 19 Requesting Studies of Japanese Political Groups and Personalities
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr., Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests all available U.S. government biographical and research material for an SCAP study of Japanese politics.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson reports the political adviser is starting a comprehensive survey of Japanese parties and personalities at SCAP's request and asks for material from State, OSS, FBI and other agencies.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Biographical Materials on Japanese Political Leaders
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.to: Acting U.S. Political Adviser to SCAP
subfiles.about: Transmits OSS, State Department, Personnel Intelligence Section, and other biographical reports.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a list of Japanese parties and members, OSS reports on political leaders and other intelligence in response to Tokyo telegram 19.

subfiles.title: Telegram Announcing Shipment of Japanese Political Biographies
subfiles.from: James F. Byrnes, Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, for George Atcheson
subfiles.about: Notifies Tokyo that biographical material on Japanese political leaders is being sent by air pouch.
subfiles.summary: Department says material on Japanese political parties will follow and offers other requested materials.

subfiles.title: Airgram Transmitting Biographical Material on Prominent Japanese
subfiles.from: James F. Byrnes, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards additional reports on prominent Japanese personalities.
subfiles.summary: Airgram sends biographical research reports with State files material, asking future requests to name individuals specifically.

subfiles.title: Airgram Transmitting a Biographical Report on Prince Fumimaro Konoe
subfiles.from: James F. Byrnes, Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Acting U.S. Political Adviser to SCAP
subfiles.about: Sends a research report and additional file information concerning Prince Fumimaro Konoe.
subfiles.summary: Airgram transmits the Interim Research and Intelligence Service's biographical report on Prince Konoe, with other Department file information.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Summary of a Plan for Reforming the Japanese Government
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Summarizes Atcheson's recommendation for replacing entrenched Japanese bureaucrats and abolishing the War and Navy ministries.
subfiles.summary: Summary of a reform plan: reactionary subordinates may obstruct reformist ministers; replace personnel in the Home and other ministries and abolish the War and Navy ministries after demobilization.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4: General Plan for Reformation of Japanese Government
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr., U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards a proposed occupation plan to overcome bureaucratic resistance to reform in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson says long-serving subordinates block reform and forwards a memorandum urging replacing reactionary personnel and abolishing the War and Navy ministries.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Supreme Commander: Reformation of Japanese Government
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr.
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander and Chief of Staff
subfiles.about: Proposes a broad purge and replacement of long-serving personnel in Japanese ministries.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson urges eliminating redundant posts, replacing half the Home Ministry's officials, overhauling Justice, Finance, monopolies and industrial associations, and abolishing the War and Navy ministries.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Organization of the Japan Socialist Party
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Summarizes Philip Sullivan's assessment of efforts to unite Japanese labor and socialist groups.
subfiles.summary: Describes Kagawa and Isoo Abe's meetings to form a moderate Japan Socialist Party, Socialist criticism of the cabinet and anti-imperial agitation after Communist prisoners' release.

subfiles.title: Moscow Telegram 3522 on Japan's Financial Oligarchy
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.about: Summarizes I. I. Polesski's Red Star article assigning war responsibility to Japanese financiers and industrialists.
subfiles.summary: Polesski rejects Japanese press arguments that only militarists were responsible for the war and that big business was a peaceful stabilizing force. He argues that the growth of Japan's major concerns was inseparable from fifty years of imperial aggression and that the financial oligarchy shared the military's guilt.

subfiles.title: Routing Note to Dean Acheson
subfiles.from: J. C. V.
subfiles.about: Calls Acheson's attention to an attached summary of Japanese political parties.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten routing note to Dean Acheson saying the November 2 résumé on pages 219-220 may interest him.

subfiles.title: Thumb-Nail Résumé of Political Parties in Japan
subfiles.from: W. T. Turner
subfiles.about: Condenses a Tokyo despatch on the Liberal, Socialist, and Communist political groupings emerging after Japan's defeat.
subfiles.summary: Résumé: prewar parties declined; defeat created the first real chance for party government. Hatoyama's Liberals conservative, Socialists seeking merger, Communists disciplined and hostile to the throne.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 17: Political Parties in Japan
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr., U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards an initial SCAP survey of Japanese political parties, personalities, objectives, and trends.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson identifies the Liberal, Socialist, and Communist groupings as the only movements then showing clear national importance. The despatch characterizes Hatoyama's Liberals as conservative, the Socialists as still divided and unorganized, and the newly released Communists as disciplined advocates of abolishing the imperial institution.

subfiles.title: Chief of Staff Memorandum Requesting a Study of Japanese Political Parties
subfiles.from: Richard K. Sutherland, Chief of Staff
subfiles.about: Directs the political adviser to study Japanese parties and submit weekly findings and recommendations.
subfiles.summary: The Supreme Commander requests analysis of party backgrounds, personalities and trends to guide peaceful government and decide who may safely participate.

subfiles.title: Memorandum Forwarding the Preliminary Report on Japanese Political Parties
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr.
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander and Chief of Staff
subfiles.about: Reports the opening of the requested political-party investigation and forwards its first preliminary report.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson forwards a preliminary report on Japanese political parties, with weekly supplements promised.

subfiles.title: Political Parties in Japan, First Filed Copy
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander and Chief of Staff
subfiles.about: Surveys the decline of prewar parties and the emerging Liberal, Socialist, Communist, and smaller political groups.
subfiles.summary: The report argues that repression and wartime totalitarian organizations destroyed effective party politics, while surrender opened an uncertain opportunity for democratic government. It analyzes Hatoyama's conservative Liberal movement, the divided Socialist coalition, and a small but disciplined Communist Party opposed to the emperor, then projects four broad future ideological blocs. An appendix lists leading personnel in the new parties, peace societies, discussion groups, and cultural associations.

subfiles.title: Political Parties in Japan, Duplicate Clear Copy
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander and Chief of Staff
subfiles.about: Duplicates the preliminary occupation report on Japanese political parties in a more legible filed copy.
subfiles.summary: This copy gives the same historical account and detailed assessment of Liberal, Socialist, and Communist organization found in the preceding report. It adds clearer biographical discussion of Hatoyama, Kagawa, Matsuoka, Katō, Tokuda, Shiga, and Nosaka and repeats the appendix of emerging parties and their personnel.

subfiles.title: Request for Declassification of Despatch No. 17
subfiles.from: Wilson C. Flake, Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.to: Originating or action division, Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Requests and records declassification of the October 15, 1945 despatch on political parties in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Declassification request: Atcheson's confidential Despatch No. 17 to be made unclassified, authorized by U. Alexis Johnson on February 1, 1952.
